claims.explanation: AM-92016 is a potassium channel blocker with weak, non-selective activity; the killing pattern is best explained by lineage/context rather than a single driver mutation. Mesothelioma and squamous/upper-aerodigestive lines are enriched among sensitive lines, while many PIK3CA/PTEN-mutant and KRAS-mutant lines are resistant, suggesting dependence on potassium-channel/NMDA-receptor-linked survival signaling in specific lineages. The virtual-cell similarity to calcium-channel and GPCR antagonists supports a polypharmacological membrane-channel mechanism rather than a single genomic biomarker.

features.basis: Mesothelioma lines (NCIH2052, MSTO211H) are selectively killed; NF2 loss is common in mesothelioma and may impair K+ channel-dependent volume regulation
PIK3CA-mutant lines (T47D, HGC27, HCC1954, KYSE70, GP2D) are mostly in the least-affected group
PTEN-mutant lines (TE4, FTC133, HEC265, GP2D) are predominantly resistant
KRAS-mutant lines (LS1034, GSU, HGC27, NCIH1792, RKN, T3M4, CL11, GP2D) are enriched among least-affected lines
NF1-mutant lines (LOXIMVI, MDAMB175VII, BICR6, S117, FTC133, GP2D, IPC298) are mostly resistant
ARID1A-mutant lines (SW1088, MDAMB175VII, T47D, HS766T, KYSE70, HEC265, GP2D) are split but enriched in resistant group
TP53 mutation is nearly universal and not discriminating; listed as context only
Annotated target of AM-92016; NMDA-receptor signaling can promote survival in neural/neuroendocrine lineages
Delayed rectifier K+ channel blockade is the annotated mechanism; expression may determine sensitivity
BK(Ca) channel activity modulates ischemic/NMDA injury; blockade exacerbates injury, so high expression may protect
HRAS-mutant lines (T24, SNU899) are among the most killed
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (K029AX, LOXIMVI) are selectively killed
